title: Microsoft Purview: sensitivity label inheritance for Teams meeting artifacts (GCC, GCC High and DoD)
summary: The roadmap details and main configuration references check out, but two statements overstate the protection mechanism. Files can also be labelled manually, and encrypted MP4 labels require admin-defined permissions rather than any encryption configuration.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans configurable inheritance of a Teams meeting's sensitivity label by recordings, transcripts and Loop notes without manual labelling.
claims.quote: Teams meeting artifacts, including recordings, transcripts, and Loop notes, can now be configured to automatically inherit the sensitivity label from the meeting.

claims.claim: The setting automatically applies the meeting's label to recordings and transcripts (.mp4) and notes (.loop) when saved to SharePoint or OneDrive.
claims.quote: automatically apply the meeting's sensitivity label to recordings and their transcripts (.mp4 files), and to meeting notes (.loop files) at the time the artifact is saved to SharePoint or OneDrive.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Later changes to the meeting label do not automatically update the inherited artifact label.
claims.quote: If the meeting label changes later, the inherited label doesn't automatically change.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; controls[1].note
claims.claim: MP4 support must be enabled for the artifact policy to label MP4 recordings.
claims.quote: If MP4 support isn't enabled, these files aren't labeled when you select this option.

claims.claim: Learn does not identify GCC, GCC High or DoD availability for the artifact setting.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams meeting artifacts sensitivity label inheritance licensing default GCC. Read sensitivity-labels-meetings and the returned GCC deployment table excerpt; neither specifies this setting's government-cloud availability.

claims.claim: Today's protection of meeting recordings and transcripts depends on someone labelling the files.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams recordings transcripts Loop notes sensitivity labels manual labeling existing protection automatic inheritance before artifacts. Read sensitivity-labels-meetings and the MP4 support section; neither establishes this blanket account of existing protection in these clouds.
claims.fix: Remove 'and today's protection depends on someone labelling the files' from the first sentence of Why it matters. The sources establish the new inheritance mechanism, not this history of existing protection.

claims.claim: Inheritance puts the same protection on artifacts, including any encryption the meeting label applies.
claims.quote: Sensitivity labels that apply encryption must be configured with the Assign permissions now option, rather than user-defined permissions.
claims.fix: Replace the second sentence of Why it matters with: 'A label that follows the meeting reduces reliance on manual artifact labelling. For MP4 files, labels that apply encryption must use Assign permissions now rather than user-defined permissions.' The existing SharePoint and OneDrive source documents this qualification.

claims.claim: Meeting recordings, transcripts and Loop notes are labelled only when a published policy applies Apply meeting label to artifacts.
claims.quote: You can, if required, manually relabel these files in SharePoint or OneDrive, by using the file's Details pane.
claims.fix: Replace the first sentence of the Data exposure bullet with: 'Apply meeting label to artifacts automatically applies the meeting label to recordings, transcripts and Loop notes when they are saved to SharePoint or OneDrive.' This states what this setting does without claiming it is the only way to label a file.
